title: People, Things & Places
description: Add identifying information about a person, thing, or place.
objectives: Add identifying information about a person, thing, or place.

stages.title: Understand the language
stages.instructions: Read the explanation, examples, common error, and recap.

blocks.text: This lesson prepares you to add identifying information about a person, thing, or place. The central language is basic relative clauses with who, that, and where. It belongs to the practical context of opinions, technology & social life. Focus first on meaning: decide what information the listener needs. Then choose the subject, verb form, and useful detail. At A2, connect the main message to a time, reason, contrast, or result. Listen for context before choosing the tense or functional phrase. The same language returns in the listening, repeat, speaking, exercises, and guided conversation stages.

blocks.title: Pattern
blocks.text: basic relative clauses with who, that, and where

blocks.english: A coworker is someone who works with you.
blocks.explanation: Use this model to begin the people, things & places exchange.

blocks.english: This is the café where we first met.
blocks.explanation: This people, things & places model adds a different detail or response.
Use this question or response to keep the people, things & places exchange moving.

blocks.text: Notice the two models: “A coworker is someone who works with you.” and “This is the café where we first met.” They show the pattern in complete communication, not as isolated grammar. Say the model aloud, replace one detail, and check that the new sentence keeps the intended meaning. When the other person asks a follow-up question, answer directly and add a relevant detail. This makes the exchange natural while keeping the language controlled. Compare the time and viewpoint in each model, and use a linker when two ideas need a clear relationship. Avoid adding advanced forms when the lesson pattern already communicates the message accurately.

blocks.title: Common error
blocks.text: Do not mix the word order or verb form with another pattern. Keep the controlled form for this lesson: basic relative clauses with who, that, and where.
